name: Safety Compute Share
summary: The lab gives a stated share of its compute or budget to safety and alignment research, and shows that it spends it.
description: Safety research needs compute that competes with product work. A stated share that others can check keeps safety work from losing when resources are short.

criteria.label: Stated Share
criteria.description: A stated share, such as a percent of compute or of the research budget.

criteria.label: Outside Research
criteria.description: Part of it goes to independent researchers, for example as grants or model access.

orgs.summary: OpenAI pledged 20% of its 2023 compute to superalignment over four years; former staff and reporters say the team got 1–2%.

events.title: Pledges 20% of compute to superalignment
events.summary: Starts the Superalignment team and says it will dedicate 20% of the compute it had secured to date, over four years, to superintelligence alignment.

quote.text: We are dedicating 20% of the compute we’ve secured to date over the next four years to solving the problem of superintelligence alignment.

events.title: Launches $10M grants for outside alignment research
events.summary: With Eric Schmidt, launches $10M in Superalignment Fast Grants for academic labs, nonprofits and individual researchers, including fellowships with compute funding.

quote.text: We’re launching $10M in grants to support technical research towards the alignment and safety of superhuman AI systems, including weak-to-strong generalization, interpretability, scalable oversight, and more.

events.title: Universities announce Superalignment Fast Grant awards
events.summary: Universities announce Superalignment Fast Grants to their researchers. Cornell reports that 50 of more than 2,700 applicants received awards.

sources.title: OpenAI funds Choudhury's work to keep superhuman AI in check
PhD Student Yihao Xue Awarded OpenAI Superalignment Fast Grant

events.title: Reports say superalignment team never got 20%
events.summary: After the Superalignment team is dissolved, Fortune cites six sources who say the team never got close to 20% of compute and that its requests for more were turned down.

sources.title: OpenAI promised 20% of its computing power to combat the most dangerous kind of AI—but never delivered

events.title: Restates 20% pledge for company-wide safety work
events.summary: Sam Altman says OpenAI is committed to giving at least 20% of its computing resources to safety efforts across the whole company. A letter to US senators makes the same promise.

quote.text: as we said last july, we're committed to allocating at least 20% of the computing resources to safety efforts across the entire company.

sources.title: OpenAI Says ‘Dedicated’ to Safety in Letter to US Lawmakers
OpenAI vows to provide the US government early access to its next AI model

events.title: Report puts superalignment compute at 1–2%
events.summary: The New Yorker cites four people who say the team's real share was one to two percent of compute, mostly on old hardware. OpenAI disputes parts of the account.

sources.title: Sam Altman May Control Our Future—Can He Be Trusted?

stated-share.commitment: States at least 20% of compute for company-wide safety work.
stated-share.missing: No public accounting; reports say the superalignment team got 1–2%.

outside-research.commitment: $10M in 2023 Superalignment Fast Grants, confirmed by grantee universities.
outside-research.missing: One round only; no stated share for outside research.

orgs.summary: Anthropic reports that about 6% of its AI R&D compute went to safety in one July 2026 week, but pledges no share.

events.title: Publishes measured share of compute for safety
events.summary: Reports that in one July 2026 week about 6% of AI R&D compute, and 12% of AI-driven R&D compute, went to safety work. It sets no target share.

quote.text: Over the examined week, about 6% of compute that went to AI R&D was allocated toward safety, and about 12% of compute that went to AI-driven AI R&D was allocated toward safety.

sources.title: Measurements for understanding the pace of AI development inside frontier labs
Anthropic shares 3 metrics to help AI companies monitor development

stated-share.commitment: Reports about 6% of AI R&D compute on safety in one July 2026 week.
stated-share.missing: No target share and no outside check.

outside-research.missing: No stated share of compute or budget for independent researchers found.

orgs.summary: Thinking Machines offers Tinker credit grants of up to $50,000 for outside safety research; it states no share of compute for safety.

events.title: Launches Tinker credit grants for safety research
events.summary: Offers grants of up to $50,000 in Tinker credits for safety research on open-weight models. Applications closed September 25; it published no total budget.

quote.text: Today, we are launching Tinker grants of up to $50,000 in credits for safety research on open-weight models.

sources.title: Safety Research Grant Program Terms & Conditions
Safety Research Grants: How to Apply

stated-share.missing: No stated share of compute or budget for safety found.

outside-research.commitment: Tinker credit grants of up to $50,000 each for open-weight safety research.
outside-research.missing: One round; no total budget, award list or outside report found.
